P1.evidence: Setter handover was acknowledged but not read back — 'I know you spoke with Kim. He kind of gave me a little bit of a head start on you' — nothing specific was reflected so the prospect could not feel seen. The frame was two-part: 'I just want to get a good idea of where you're at. Really build out what it is that you want and what it is that you want to accomplish. Then if everything aligns, we can talk about the coaching. And if not, that's fine as well.' Missing 'what's in the way' and 'what you need'. Agreement was requested and given — 'Okay?' / 'Okay, good.' The open question ran: 'let's kick off with what were you hoping we could potentially help with?'

P2.evidence: In 32 minutes the rep never asked age, height, weight, occupation, training frequency, results, sleep or energy. Occupation is the standout omission on a call where the ICP screens on it. Health and injury were touched only inside the pitch, not discovery, and only as a request for paperwork: 'If you have any specific diagnoses, that'd be good. Like if you have a herniated disc, for example, right? Tell us all that information.' Duration and history of the back problem were never asked. Nutrition was asked as a need question rather than a baseline question — 'do you feel like you need help with that or no?' — and the actual diet (low-fat Mediterranean, vegetable-heavy) was volunteered 15 minutes later. Everything material about this prospect's body arrived unprompted.

P3.evidence: No goals phase was run at all. The rep never went past the presenting request. The only reflection was a surface restatement: 'So you want to essentially make everything more efficient, be able to do it from home and do it with kettlebells and with body weight.' The prospect handed over two deep threads unprompted and both were dropped — the young child ('we have a little one, so my free time is reduced tremendously', and he ends the call for 'my daddy activities') and a decade-plus longevity horizon ('my goal is to do this for the next decade or so... it needs to adapt with me'). Neither was followed with 'who else does that impact' or driven through to family or legacy. This is the single biggest coachable gap on the call.

P4.evidence: The prospect delivered a complete past-attempts history unprompted in his opening answer — CrossFit causing injuries, bodybuilding causing stiffness, yoga being insufficient — and the rep asked none of it and probed none of it. No 'why do you feel it didn't stick', no 'what's the one thing getting in the way', no naming of the structural gap. Volunteered information earns no credit.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame. Nothing about the next two years, no test of willingness to settle, no line in the sand — despite an unusually strong available frame: a man with worsening stiffness, active back and hip pain, and a young child, who himself said 'age is not a very nice mistress'. The rep moved from discovery straight into product mechanics.

P6.evidence: No commitment check of any kind. The first price was quoted at 00:11:19 with no verbal yes secured, and the rep prefaced it by arguing against his own offer: 'So I don't think the coaching is going to be the best thing for you.' The prospect never confirmed he believed the programme could get him there, and the whole back half of the call ran on unresolved doubt.

P11.evidence: No close was attempted. The rep never asked for the sale, never proposed taking payment, and ended by agreeing to send a note-taker summary and wait for the prospect's list of injuries. Payment, the Trevor onboarding call, the agreement email and the Skool/welcome steps were never reached.

objection_plays.detail: Fear/doubt trigger is unmistakable at 00:24:59 — 'How much can you adjust for injuries? That's a bit the tricky one' — followed by 'if I'm not feeling comfortable throughout it, then I just need to stop' and 'I might not be even like a good fit'. The rep ran an unscripted relatability move ('here's the thing, I've got scoliosis, I work out with kettlebells') and a risk-reduction move (drop to the one-month term). None of the scripted moves ran: no 'would it be fair to say you're looking for certainty', no pleasure/pain question, no bridge, plane or burned-before frame, and no 'how will you know if you never actually try'. The doubt was reduced by shrinking the purchase rather than resolved.

Delay trigger at 00:28:14 — 'gear went until the weekend... there's no urgency on your side. So you can even come back to me next week.' The rep not only failed to run the play, he accepted and reinforced the delay by agreeing to route the prospect's list to Trevor first. No 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you there', no 'what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is'.

No money objection arose at any point. The prospect absorbed $6,000/6mo, $9,000/12mo and the franc and euro equivalents without a single affordability remark, and rejected the cheap self-guided tier on principle rather than reaching for it. Correctly not run — but it also means the rep spent the call solving a price problem the prospect did not have.

Script gap — clinical fit, the known gap, in its most acute form yet. The prospect disclosed that kettlebell swings are currently causing him lower back pain and that a mid-back issue is driving lower back and hip issues, then asked directly whether the programme could adapt. There is no scripted path here, and what the rep improvised made it worse: he pushed the prospect away from the local physio ('it wouldn't be worth it if you still had a nutritionist and still had the physio') and substituted his own scoliosis anecdote for a clinical question. The script needs a mandatory clearance gate, not a better rebuttal.

Script gap — unbundling. The prospect twice asked to buy training and mobility without nutrition because he already has a nutrition practitioner and a conflicting dietary approach: 'is there a way for you to check to offload the nutrition out of it'. No scripted play exists. The rep held the bundle firmly and consistently, which is the right commercial answer, and pre-empted it with the three-pillars-as-a-system argument. Marked hit for the improvisation, but the script should own this — it recurs whenever a prospect already has a practitioner.

Script gap — dietary philosophy mismatch. Prospect follows a low-fat, vegetable-heavy Mediterranean diet against a red-meat-and-eggs-forward programme. The rep handled it well with vegan and Indian vegetarian social proof and a tailoring promise, and the prospect accepted, but nothing in the playbook covers it and the promise was never made specific.

notes: Thirty-two minutes and the process barely ran: no goals phase, no past-attempts phase, no consequence frame, no commitment check, and the first price quoted at the eleven-minute mark into an untested commitment. The prospect handed over a young child, a decade-long horizon and a body in pain, and none of it was developed. Two specific things to coach: never quote a number before a verbal yes, and never tell a prospect with active spinal pain that keeping his physio makes the coaching not worth buying.
